import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class I {

    public static boolean DEBUG = true;
    public static String name = "I";

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        FastScanner scan;
        PrintWriter out;
        if (DEBUG) {
            scan = new FastScanner(System.in);
            out = new PrintWriter(System.out);
        } else {
            scan = new FastScanner(name + ".in");
            out = new PrintWriter(new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(name + ".out")));
        }

        int N = Integer.parseInt(scan.nextString());
        double P = Double.parseDouble(scan.nextString());

        // Handle edge cases
        if (P <= 0) {
            out.println(0);
            out.close();
            return;
        }
        if (P >= 1) {
            out.println(N);
            out.close();
            return;
        }

        // Try each possible number of maps to study (i)
        for (int i = 0; i <= N; i++) {
            double probability = calculateProbability(N, i);
            if (probability >= P) {
                out.println(i);
                break;
            }
        }

        out.close();
    }

    // Calculate probability that at least one studied map is selected
    public static double calculateProbability(int N, int studied) {
        if (studied == 0) return 0.0;
        if (studied >= N) return 1.0;

        // Total ways to choose 3 maps from N
        long totalWays = (long) N * (N - 1) * (N - 2) / 6;

        // Count favorable cases: at least one studied map in the final selected map
        // Instead, calculate probability that the final map is NOT studied and subtract from 1
        // Final map is not studied only if:
        // 1. All 3 shown maps include 0 or 1 studied maps
        // 2. Both players discard all studied maps shown (if any)

        // Better approach: Calculate probability that the final map is studied
        // Case analysis based on how many studied maps are in the initial 3 shown

        double prob = 0.0;

        // Case 0: 0 studied maps shown (all 3 are unstudied)
        // Probability of this case: C(N-studied, 3) / C(N, 3)
        // Final map will be unstudied, so contributes 0 to success probability
        if (N - studied >= 3) {
            long case0 = (long) (N - studied) * (N - studied - 1) * (N - studied - 2) / 6;
            // prob += 0 * case0/totalWays;
        }

        // Case 1: 1 studied map shown, 2 unstudied
        // Number of ways: C(studied, 1) * C(N-studied, 2)
        // Players must discard the unstudied ones to have the studied map survive
        // Each player randomly picks one of 3 maps to discard
        // For the studied map to be selected, both players must discard unstudied maps
        // There are 2 unstudied maps, each player picks one to discard
        // Cases where both discard unstudied: 
        //   - Both discard same unstudied map: 2 ways (both discard map A, or both discard map B)
        //   - Each discards different unstudied map: 2 ways (player1 discards A, player2 discards B; or vice versa)
        // Total favorable: 4 out of 3*3=9 possible discard combinations
        if (studied >= 1 && N - studied >= 2) {
            long case1 = (long) studied * (N - studied) * (N - studied - 1) / 2;
            double successProb1 = 4.0 / 9.0;
            prob += case1 * successProb1 / totalWays;
        }

        // Case 2: 2 studied maps shown, 1 unstudied
        // Number of ways: C(studied, 2) * C(N-studied, 1)
        // For at least one studied map to be selected:
        // - If both players discard the unstudied map, then one studied map is randomly selected (success)
        // - If one player discards unstudied and the other discards studied, then the remaining studied map is selected (success)
        // - If both players discard studied maps, then the unstudied map is selected (failure)
        // Let's enumerate all 9 combinations:
        // Maps: S1, S2, U
        // Player1 choices: S1, S2, U; Player2 choices: S1, S2, U
        // Success cases: 
        //   - P1 discards U, P2 discards U: remaining {S1,S2}, random pick → success
        //   - P1 discards U, P2 discards S1: remaining {S2,U}, but P2 discarded S1, so system picks from {S2,U} not discarded by anyone? Wait, re-read problem.
        // Actually: "The game system then randomly selects one of the maps that were not picked by any of the players"
        // So if P1 discards U and P2 discards S1, then maps not discarded: S2 (P1 kept S2, P2 kept S2), so S2 is selected → success
        // Similarly: P1 discards U, P2 discards S2 → S1 selected → success
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards U → S2 selected → success
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards U → S1 selected → success
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S2 → U selected → failure
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S1 → U selected → failure
        // P1 discards S1, P2 discards S1 → remaining {S2,U}, system picks randomly → 0.5 success
        // P1 discards S2, P2 discards S2 → remaining {S1,U}, system picks randomly → 0.5 success
        // P1 discards U, P2 discards U → remaining {S1,S2}, system picks randomly → success
        // So success cases: 6 cases with 1.0 success + 2 cases with 0.5 success = 6 + 1 = 7 out of 9
        if (studied >= 2 && N - studied >= 1) {
            long case2 = (long) studied * (studied - 1) / 2 * (N - studied);
            double successProb2 = 7.0 / 9.0;
            prob += case2 * successProb2 / totalWays;
        }

        // Case 3: 3 studied maps shown
        // Number of ways: C(studied, 3)
        // All maps are studied, so whatever is selected is a success
        if (studied >= 3) {
            long case3 = (long) studied * (studied - 1) * (studied - 2) / 6;
            prob += case3 * 1.0 / totalWays;
        }

        return prob;
    }

    static class FastScanner {

        InputStream dis;
        byte[] buffer = new byte[1 << 17];
        int pointer = 0;

        public FastScanner(String fileName) throws IOException {
            dis = new FileInputStream(fileName);
        }

        public FastScanner(InputStream is) throws IOException {
            dis = is;
        }

        int nextInt() throws IOException {
            int ret = 0;

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            boolean negative = false;
            if (b == '-') {
                negative = true;
                b = nextByte();
            }
            while (b >= '0' && b <= '9') {
                ret = 10 * ret + b - '0';
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return (negative) ? -ret : ret;
        }

        long nextLong() throws IOException {
            long ret = 0;

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            boolean negative = false;
            if (b == '-') {
                negative = true;
                b = nextByte();
            }
            while (b >= '0' && b <= '9') {
                ret = 10 * ret + b - '0';
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return (negative) ? -ret : ret;
        }

        byte nextByte() throws IOException {
            if (pointer == buffer.length) {
                dis.read(buffer, 0, buffer.length);
                pointer = 0;
            }
            return buffer[pointer++];
        }

        String nextString() throws IOException {
            StringBuffer ret = new StringBuffer();

            byte b;
            do {
                b = nextByte();
            } while (b <= ' ');
            while (b > ' ') {
                ret.appendCodePoint(b);
                b = nextByte();
            }

            return ret.toString();
        }

    }
}
